# Automated Testing and Repair for Verified Compilers Generated by a Coding Agent
(authored by agents unless marked 🧑)
Tag: `rinard2026automated`, [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28928)

ACDC: agent-based test + repair for Axon, an agent-generated verified Lean compiler
- 4 code kinds: verified, checked, unverified, specification
- proofs conditional on faithful semantics, checker, Lean kernel, generated code
differential ASM testing: run random ASM on executable semantics vs printed+assembled code
- batches of 6-32 instructions, fresh seed each, immediates 1/3 random, 2/3 extremal
- classes: Match, Different Outcome, Assemble Fail, Panic; record seed + diff
- 30 min detect: 8,200 programs, 82% hit a defect
  - 5 repairs: 3 printer, 1 semantics, 1 both
  - 2nd phase: 4,600 programs, 0 defects
- Verus analogue: exec Rust model vs emitted-asm run as test oracle only
  - does not certify assembler or hardware
certificate-rejection testing for credible compilation
- checker rejection causes: unsound transform, bad certificate, too-tight checker
- 3 generators in sequence: Csmith-style typed random, skeleton variants, EMI variants
- repair agent must reproduce trigger, localize fault, audit all proof consumers, validate on new programs
- 13 defects repaired
  - e.g. dead-edge handling, divide-dividend check, unreachable-point obligations
- checker relaxation needs a re-proved soundness lemma
parser/printer round trip for unverified interfaces
- generate typed ASTs, print, parse, compare AST equality
- 13.77M programs all failed at first declaration
  - 4 repairs, then 18.08M programs with 0 defects
- targets consistency, not malformed-input parser bugs
